definitions.explanation: A large beetle with distinctive mandibles that resemble deer antlers. Popular among Japanese children as collectible insects.

examples.japanese: {夏休|なつやす}みに{山|やま}でクワガタムシを{捕|つか}まえた。
examples.english: I caught a stag beetle in the mountains during summer vacation.

examples.japanese: クワガタムシは{夜行性|やこうせい}だ。
{息子|むすこ}がクワガタムシを{飼|か}いたがっている。
examples.english: My son wants to keep a stag beetle as a pet.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The name comes from {鍬形|くわがた} (hoe-shaped decoration on samurai helmets) + {虫|むし} (insect), referring to the beetle's large mandibles that resemble this decoration.

ABBREVIATION:
Often shortened to クワガタ in casual speech.

POPULAR HOBBY:
Collecting and raising stag beetles ({昆虫|こんちゅう}{採集|さいしゅう}) is a beloved summer activity for Japanese children. They are often kept alongside カブトムシ (rhinoceros beetles).

COMMON SPECIES:
・オオクワガタ (giant stag beetle) - the most prized species
・ノコギリクワガタ (saw stag beetle)
・ミヤマクワガタ (deep mountain stag beetle)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・クワガタムシを{飼|か}う (to keep a stag beetle)
・クワガタムシを{捕|つか}まえる (to catch a stag beetle)
・クワガタムシの{幼虫|ようちゅう} (stag beetle larva)
・クワガタムシの{餌|えさ} (stag beetle food - usually tree sap or jelly)
